newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - APRIL 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - APRIL 3.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:
KATHIMERINI
--The finance ministry is to begin implementation of the new code on fines for outstanding taxes within the next few months, in an attempt to improve the standing of tax revenues for the state.
--The government will have made the final decisions on how to define price levels for pharmaceuticals and the level of state spending by the middle of next month.

--The Ionian Bank will distribute bonus shares folllowing an announcement that it has more than doubled its profits in the first two months of this year in comparison to last year. The unsatisfactory course of the bank in 1996 has been turned around, bank president Haris Stamatopoulos said yesterday.
--Finance ministry employees will be the first to receive their wages through banks this June: the procedure will be extended to all civil servants and to pensioners.
IMERISIA

--The government is planning on re-examining the category of taxes imposed on third parties as it deems the system to be creating deviations in the market and particularly in the definition of prices and, subsequently, hindering the fall of inflation.
--The Athens Stock Exchange yesterday saw its general price index rise 1.67 percent to close at 1,375.10 points: low returns from the banking market are the most important factor suporting prices.
--Deputy Commerce Minister Mihalis Chrysohoidis will broach the issue of granting of credit cards at his meeting with the Association of Greek Banks.
KERDOS

--The redistribution of Community funds not only to other projects but to other sectors is expected to be decided upon at today's meeting of the Community Support Framework monitoring committee. The government, according to sources, is pressing for the need to transfer funds from projects irretrievably 'stuck' to more viable ones.

--Greece will stick to its 'hard drachma' policy until the country enters European Economic and Monetary Union, National Economy and Finance Minister Yannos Papandoniou is expected to tell his EU counterparts in Brussels on Friday.
--Greece's Gross Domestic Product has seen a slight rate of improvement in 1996 over 1995 figures, according to Eurostat.
NAFTEMBORIKI

--Prime Minister Costas Simitis yesterday presented his image of the worker of the 21st century to his ruling PASOK MPs while new opposition leader, New Democracy president Costas Karamanlis, told his MPs that the government was guilty of a "revenue-gathering mentality".
--The market bid 1.66 trillion drachmas, way over the central bank's offer of 250 billion drachmas, in yesterday's fixed rate depo tender. The auction related to 14-day funds at 11.9 percent.
--Transfers of funds from bank to bank for clients will be simplified under the new system being created by the "Dias" company.
EXPRESS
--The much-awaited tax crimes squad (SDOE) will begin operating in April, with the first target the wholesale and retail trade, and industry.
--Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
